fit: coffee and tea as candidate factors in a young-stroke case-control report
assessment: The 1985 abstract lists coffee and tea together among candidate factors. It gives no coffee-specific estimate and does not measure Parkinson fatigue.

fit: coffee in the historical differential of paroxysmal movement attacks
assessment: The authors discuss coffee in the alternative diagnosis. The described five-person family's episodes are movement-triggered. The member does not establish a coffee effect in the five cases or in Parkinson fatigue.

fit: self-reported beverage-associated attacks in a familial dyskinesia pedigree
assessment: Coffee and black or green tea were reported as attack triggers in the Japanese family. Roasted green tea did not trigger the reported attacks. The cohort has familial episodic dyskinesia, with no Parkinson fatigue endpoint.

fit: reported caffeine triggers in familial episodic dyskinesia
assessment: The authors distinguish triggers across genotyped family groups. The abstract has no separately assigned brewed coffee test or Parkinson fatigue outcome. Independence of all families relative to the historical literature remains unverified.

fit: chicken tissue myosin, taurine and enzyme comparisons in separate conference members
assessment: The chicken results concern extracted muscle and animal disease. The human biopsy report refers to an earlier chicken tissue comparison. None measures fatigue after eating poached chicken.

fit: referenced chicken muscle and taurine comparison
assessment: The conference member cites the chapter to identify chicken muscle fibre composition. Its full chapter methods and tables are unverified. The exposure is a tissue sample.

fit: chicken muscle oxidative enzyme activity and development
assessment: The original abstract measures enzyme activity and reactive products in dystrophic chicken tissues. It provides no dietary comparator.

fit: additional chicken pectoral muscle enzyme outcomes
assessment: The same research program measures other enzymes in groups of developing chickens. Sample overlap with the conference report remains open.

fit: later chicken dystrophy enzyme study
assessment: Raised enzyme activity in tissues describes avian disease. The later report may share animals or experiments with the 1985 material. No intake endpoint is measured.
